reasons.demand: Measured (Keyword Planner, Oct 2024-Sep 2026, exported 2026-10-24): 3,800 searches/month in Michigan across 43 queries, 22 with any volume, none above Google's 500 bucket; 14,600/month US. Every harbor-specific and safety phrase shows no volume; people search by lake and metric. Under the 5k yardstick = weak.
reasons.repeat_use: Boaters, anglers, paddlers and beach-goers check conditions every outing in season; water level draws year-round interest. Winter is thin because buoys are out.
reasons.competition: Nick's incognito check: top results are NOAA's own marine forecast text pages, dated-looking and one metric per page. Page-level competition is weak, but the competitor is the authoritative government source, which is hard to outrank.
reasons.license: All public domain (NDBC, CO-OPS, NWS, GLERL), no keys, verified live at G0. GLOS skipped and Open-Meteo not used per Nick (free tier non-commercial; Standard tier about USD 29/month, not paying).
reasons.build_effort: core.fetch pulls all feeds and refresh.py builds a page; 1-2 weeks for a location table, static-site loop, hourly schedule and hosting. Smaller still if the design pivots to 6 per-lake pages.

decision_reason: Total 18/25. Demand evidence is weak (score 2), so no GO despite the total. Consider merging with river-levels.
